Commentary.Commentary: The pitch has played superbly so far. It has looked a good one for stroke making and South Africa will back themselves to overhaul this below-par target. Having said that, their batting has been quite disappointing in this series. However, with Faf du Plessis returning in the mix, things would be different. The hosts were yearning for some batting practice and today they have enough runs to test themselves. Let's see how they fare in the run chase. Do join us in a short while.

Sean Williams feels it is a good surface. Stresses that if the batsmen play themselves in, they get a chance to score big. On the improved batting performance today, Sean says that the message in the dressing room was to come out of a shell and express oneself. Admits that throughout the series, the top 6 were not contributing and they aimed that today. Adds that they targeted Shamsi, not giving any wicket in his first few overs and it worked for them. Is not too confident about 228 being a decent total but feels if they can pick up some early wickets, they have a chance.

For the visiting side, Sean Williams was the best batsman on show and he looked at ease against the South African bowling. He was particularly severe on Tabraiz Shamsi as he smashed him with a strike rate well in excess of 125. His departure was a big blow for the Zimbabweans. He is giving an interview to Shaun Pollock, let's see what he has to say...

Just when Zimbabwe started to recover from the early loss of wickets, Imran Tahir's beautiful leggie got Taylor stumped. Post that, the wickets continued to tumble, although runs also kept coming. Towards the end, Donald Tiripano was involved in handy stands with the lower order, courtesy which Zimbabwe managed to cross the 200-run mark. Dale Steyn and Kagiso Rabada bowled superbly to pick 3 wickets apiece while Imran Tahir was also impressive. Andile Phehlukwayo bounced back well in his second spell after going for aplenty in his first but Tabraiz Shamsi looked completely off-colour and got his worst bowling spell in ODIs.

A much-improved batting show by Zimbabwe today. However, it didn't start in a good manner. Dale Steyn was in excellent rhythm at the beginning and along with Imran Tahir (first time sharing the new ball), he pegged the visiting side back early. They were reeling on 44/3 at one stage but then the 73-run partnership between Brendan Taylor and Sean Williams bailed them out. The pair batted with good control and mixed caution with aggression in its approach.

OUT! Third wicket for Steyn as well! Steyn digs in a shorter length ball outside off at 138 kph, Tiripano hangs back and once again tries to power it over the off side. But this time he fails to get enough pump behind his shot and du Plessis moves across to his left at extra cover to collect an easy catch. End of a handy knock by Donald Tiripano. ZIMBABWE ARE ALL OUT FOR 228!
A length ball angling into the batsman, Tiripano goes hard at it but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
FOUR! Wonderful start to the over! Back of a length delivery around off, Donald makes room and whacks it over extra cover for a boundary.
Full toss on middle, Chatara pushes down through mid on and comes out looking for a run. He is sent back as Donald Tiripano wants to face the final over.
Tendai Chatara is the last batsman.

OUT! Jarvis holes out! Rabada hurls in a slower length ball around off, at 115 kph, Kyle targets the long on fence and goes hard at it. Fails to middle his shot properly and is caught in the deep by Phehlukwayo. Third wicket for KG!
An off pace delivery, shortish and around off, Donald punches it early and it goes a bit aerially towards covers. One run added to the total.
Follows the batsman down the leg side with a short delivery, Tiripano tries pulling but misses.
Shortish and wide outside off, slapped down the ground to long off for one.
Short in length and around off, Jarvis powers his hook to deep mid-wicket for a couple of runs. Good work in the deep by Duminy.
Another shorter one, a mistimed pull shot fell towards mid-wicket and the fielder inside the ring quickly got to it. Dot to end the over.
Shortish delivery, forced down to long on for a run.
Short and wide outside off, Jarvis tries to smash it over the off side but misses. No yorker attempted yet by Steyn.
Remains inside the crease to a good length delivery and punches it to point.
Slower in pace this time, an off cutter at 120 kph, Tiripano stays back and works it nicely to third man for a run.
Heavy ball, on a length and around off, Tiripano defends it off his back foot.
Shortish and outside off, Jarvis once again tries to slam it over the off side but misses. 7 from the over.

FOUR! Makes proper connection this time. Picks the slower one early, it's on a length around off, Jarvis throws the kitchen sink on it and powers it over mid on. No one in the deep and it's a boundary.
Outside off, Jarvis swings and misses.
Shortish and on off, Tiripano plays it down to third man for a run.

DROPPED! A slower length ball around off, Tiripano clears his front leg and swings it across the line. Fails to middle his shot and it balloons in the air towards deep mid-wicket. Andile Phehlukwayo runs back from the ring, keeps his eyes on the ball and tries to catch it but it slips out from his fingers. The ball rolls towards the fence but the fielder in the deep reaches to it and stops it from committing the crime. Two runs taken.
Shortish and on off, Donald goes on his toes and plays it down to point.
Kagiso Rabada is back on.
No yorker. Again a short delivery wide outside off, Kyle tries his best to put bat on ball but misses.
Another short delivery, wide outside off, Jarvis flashes and misses. A yorker seems imminent.
Another bouncer, Jarvis ducks. Is Steyn setting him up for a yorker?
Effort delivery by Dale. Bends his back and digs in a short ball, Jarvis ducks immediately.
Swing and a miss! Steyn bowls a slower one outside off, the length is on the shorter side and Jarvis tries to hit it hard. Only manages to connect with thin air.
Clips it off his pads to deep square leg for a run.
Dale Steyn is back to bowl at the death.
Bouncer this time, Andile mixing up his length, Jarvis ducks to let one through.
Very full delivery first up for the new batsman, Jarvis digs it out back to the bowler.
Kyle Jarvis is in next.

OUT! A soft dismissal! Phehlukwayo takes the pace off this delivery but fails to land it. Mavuta sees the full toss and backs himself to clear the fence. But he doesn't account for the lack of speed and as a result top edges it towards mid off. A simple catch for the fit-again skipper, Faf du Plessis. End of a vital knock and a 28-run partnership.
Full and angling into the batsman, Mavuta jumps out of the crease for a big swing over the leg side. But it takes the inside edge and speeds down to fine leg for a couple.
Width on offer outside off, it's run down to third man for a run.
Angles in a length ball on middle, Tiripano gets behind the line and defends it back.
Loopy full delivery around leg, it's reverse swept through point for a single. Shamsi finishes his most expensive spell in ODIs, 10-0-72-0!
The batsman plays a sweep shot. They pick up a single.
Flighted around leg, Brandon brings his bat down just in time to keep it out.
Another edgy shot! Mavuta goes for the reverse sweep to a googly and top edges it over the first slip fielder. A couple more added to the total.
Three byes! When it's not your day, it's just not your day. Shamsi bowls the googly, it beats the batsman but also the keeper. It rolls behind and they take three.
Tossed up ball on off, defended off the front foot.
FOUR! Slapped away! Short in length and outside off, Mavuta rocks back and spanks it through the line. It's aerial but speeds past the diving du Plessis at wide mid off.
Turns a length ball softly in the gap at mid-wicket for a run.
Beaten! Shortish and around off, slower in pace, Donald swishes and misses.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, Mavuta swings his bat blindly and gets a bottom edge. It rolls behind and Klaasen does well to make the stop.
Prods forward to a full ball and defends it. 11 from the over, Shamsi's figures today, 9-0-68-0!
FOUR! Good shot! Shamsi flights it up and lands it outside off, Tiripano gets down for the reverse sweep, takes it on the full and nails it past first slip for a boundary.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
In the air... safe! Tossed up ball around leg, Mavuta top edges his attempted slog sweep and it falls in front of the deep square leg fielder. They take a run.
FOUR! Shamsi has not been spared today. Hurls it very full and on middle, Mavuta clears his front leg and muscles it over mid on for a boundary.
Goes down on one knee and sweeps it towards short fine leg where Rabada misfields and allows the extra run. Two added to the total.
Gets bat on ball and steers it through point for a run. End of a successful over by Andile, just 1 from it along with the wicket of Chigumbura.
Slower delivery again. A bit short around off and holding its line, Mavuta throws his bat at it and misses. Nearly another edge in the over.
Bowls it on a driving length outside off, Mavuta goes hard at it and mistimes his attempted shot.
Lands it full and outside off, it's pushed out to covers.
Mavuta has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Brandon Mavuta is the new batsman.

OUT! Oh yes, Phehlukwayo redeems himself by striking first ball. He lets out a harmless short of a length delivery wide outside off. It's bowled at 123 kph and Chigumbura rocks back to slap it square of the wicket on the off side. But he probably is beaten due to the slowness of the delivery. Flashes early and nicks it behind to Klaasen. Third catch for the keeper along with a stumping. He is also having a good game.
Powerplay 3 signalled. Andile Phehlukwayo is back into the attack. He has proved expensive today. Can he redeem himself in this spell?
Comes from 'round the wicket and bowls a flighted ball on middle. Tiripano defends it off his front foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Vital runs coming from Donald's bat! Tahir bowls a googly but it's on the shorter side. Tiripano gets the opportunity go back and power it over mid on. The fielder is inside the ring and hence a boundary results.
Googly, landing full outside off and turning back in, Donald defends it off his front foot.
FOUR! Easily done! Turning down the leg side, Tiripano just deflects it fine to earn himself a boundary.
Loopy full ball on middle, Tiripano brings down a straight bat in defense.
Fullish and on off, pushed off the inner half of the bat to mid on.
Shortish and on off, played down with an angled bat to backward point.
Bouncer around off, Chigumbura ducks underneath it.
Elton has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, tapped down to point.
Play and a miss! Short and wide outside off, Chigumbura flashes at it and misses.
A googly around off, spinning back in, Donald is forward in defense.
FOUR! The length is short this time and Tiripano goes on the back foot to pummel it through covers for a boundary.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Flighted and off, defended off the front foot.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Gets forward to a full ball and defends it watchfully.

A stifled appeal, more of an inquiry. Rabada digs in a short ball, targeting the rib cage of the batsman, Donald tries to sway away awkwardly and it goes behind off something as there is noise. The keeper collects it and appeals but nothing from the umpire. The sound was of the ball brushing his arm-guard.
Movement back into the batsman, Chigumbura keeps it out off the inside half of the bat to square leg for a run.
Bouncer, too high and it's called a wide.
FOUR! Rabada is very full and on middle, Chigumbura leans forward and across before flicking it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Shortish and on off, defended off the back foot to the off side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Another wide. An attempted yorker gone wrong. It's down the leg side. Elton fails to make any use of it.
Wide! Slips a low full toss around leg and angling down, Elton fails to flick and the keeper has done well to collect it to his left.
Tossed up ball on off, pushed off the front foot through covers. A single to end the over.
Pulls back his length and bowls it on off, Chigumbura goes back and punches it to covers.
Strides forward to a full ball and defends it with the spin to point.
A full toss this time, it has been pushed back to the bowler.
A slower googly landing full on off, Elton picks it and defends it off his front foot.
Loopy and full on off, Chigumbura defends it by getting forward.
Wide! Quicker and fuller but down the leg side. Elton tries sweeping but misses.
Imran Tahir is back on.
A length ball on off, angling in, Tiripano defends it to point.
Donald Tiripano is the new batsman.

OUT! Sean Williams is gone! That's a body blow to Zimbabwe. Rabada with the breakthrough. He spears in a length ball on middle, maybe coming a bit slower off the deck as Sean tries to flick it on the leg side. But he fails to close the face of the bat in time and ends up chipping the ball back to the bowler. Rabada stretches to his left to catch the ball and that ends a fine knock. Can Zimbabwe get to 200 from here?
Beaten comprehensively. That's a brilliant delivery. Rabada steams in from 'round the wicket and angles in a shortish ball around middle and off, Williams stays back to defend but is beaten for pace.
Shortish and on off, Williams moves back and taps it down to cover-point.
A length ball closer to the off stump line, not enough room on offer as Chigumbura  tries to force the issue through covers but gets an inside edge past the stumps to fine leg. A single taken.
Back of a length ball on off, Elton goes on the back foot and defends it to covers.
Kagiso Rabada is back on.
Extra flight this time, it lands full on off, Chigumbura tries to drive but it spins back in to gather the inside edge. The ball rolls to square leg and they switch ends.
Wide! Goes quicker this time but fails to control his line. It's down the leg side and the batsman fails to connect with his sweep shot.
Tossed up ball on middle, Elton defends it by bringing his bat close to the front pad. Had he missed, he was dead in front.
Full and flighted on off, Chigumbura drives it straight to short extra cover.
Full and on off, knocked down through mid off for a run.

FOUR! Smashing shot! Picking the length of Shamsi has been the highlight of Williams' innings so far. He once again picks the shorter one in a trice, goes deep inside the crease and crunches his square cut through point.
Flighted and full on off, Sean leans forward in defense.

Steyn alters his length and spears in a very full ball around off, Elton does well to keep it out. Just a run and a wicket from the over. Another good spell this by Steyn, he is doing the damage for South Africa.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Good length ball around off, staying a bit low, Chigumbura defends it off his back foot.
As the players are taking Drinks, Elton Chigumbura has joined Williams in the middle.

OUT! Believe me, this is an outstanding catch. Reeza Hendricks made that look so easy, it's never so at slips. The eagerness to steal a run from third man has brought Peter's downfall. Steyn delivers it on the shorter side outside off, at 143 kph, Moor opens the face of his blade as he tries to run it down but ends up chipping it behind. Hendricks leaps across to his left and grabs it nicely. Another developing partnership has been nipped in the bud. Peter's innings is no more now.
A length ball on middle, blocked from the crease by Peter.
Shortish and angling away, Williams dabs it down to third man for a run.

SIX! This has gone all the way, the first biggie of this match. Moor reads the variation well there. He spots it to be spinning back in and heaves it across the line with full power. Makes fine connection and it sails over the head of the fielder standing near the rope at deep mid-wicket. They are attacking the chinaman here. 11 from the over after a maiden by Steyn. Pressure releasing one!
Loopy ball around leg, turning down, Moor goes back and hits it straight to mid-wicket.
Yet another short delivery around off, Sean punches it down to long off for a run.
Tossed up ball on off, forced from the back foot to covers.
Flatter and shorter on off, turning away again, Williams rocks back to punch it through the line but mistimes it.
FOUR! Another nicely executed shot! Shamsi serves it full and around off, turning away, Williams kneels down and slog sweeps it in front of square leg. It nearly went all the way.
Play and a miss! Speedy delivery, a touch short and outside off, Moor tries to play the square cut but is beaten for pace. Maiden over by Steyn, a good pressure-building one.
Back of a length delivery on off, the batsman jumps on his back foot and taps it down to point.
Moor has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Another delivery which has been angled in around off, Peter defends it watchfully to covers.
On a length and around off, Moor defends it off his front foot to the off side.
Bends his back and lets out a shortish ball outside off, Moor leans back a bit and leaves it alone.

Nearly hit it straight down the throat of Khaya Zondo. Shamsi drags his length short and bowls it on middle, Moor pushes himself deep inside the crease and lofts it over square leg. It goes on one bounce to deep square leg. Good that he didn't time it well there. They pick up a single.
Goes on the back foot and punches it through point for a run.

FOUR! Well played! Shamsi serves it flatter and fuller around off, spinning away after landing, Sean gets down on one knee, gets on top of the bounce and bludgeons his reverse sweep through backward point. This is now Sean Williams' highest ODI score against South Africa.
Flighted and on off, turning away, Moor pushes it with an angled bat through cover-point for a run.
Too full and on off, driven firmly to the off side but straight to the cover fielder.
Floated and full on off, pushed back to the bowler who dived across to his right to stop the ball.
Back of a length delivery on off, pulling back his pace a bit and bowls it at 132 kph. Williams goes back to punch but fails to gather enough power or timing. Finds covers.
Touches 140 kph and serves a length ball in line of the middle stump, Williams covers the line and blocks it solidly to the off side.
Good length ball around leg, Williams plays it off his pads to square leg.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
A touch short and on middle and leg, Williams nudges it through square leg for one.
Fullish and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Dale Steyn is back on.

DROPPED! A tough chance but should have been taken. Shamsi delivers it in line of the stumps and gets it to curve away. Williams is opened up in defense and ends up edging it behind. Faf du Plessis at first slip reacts quickly to his right but fails to grab the catch. A life for Williams soon after reaching a half century. Can he make it count?

FOUR! Another boundary for Williams and he brings up his 28th ODI fifty. Shamsi once again is on the shorter side with his length and this time Sean pulls it with authority in front of square leg for a boundary. Fine knock by him so far but Zimbabwe need a big one from him.
FOUR! Bang! Shamsi drags his length short around off and after that it doesn't matter which way it's spinning. Williams rocks back, gets enough time to pull it and has nailed it through mid-wicket.
Beaten! Bowls it flat and a touch short on off, Williams tries playing at it but it spins away to beat the outside edge.
Turning away from the batsman, Williams commits himself early onto the front foot as he goes for the drive. Fails to control his shot and plays it aerially through covers. A couple taken.
Tossed up ball on off, Williams defends it off his front foot.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. End of a successful over.
Full and on middle, flicked through square leg for one.
Turning away from the batsman, Moor pushes it with gentle hands and gets it away off the outer half of the bat towards point. A single taken.
Flighted and on off, defended back off the front foot.
Peter Moor walks out to the middle. A slip in place for him.

OUT! Dear me, Taylor's back foot is in the air when the stumps are disturbed. A bit unfortunate for Brendan but credit to the bowler for deceiving him with the turn. Also, Klaasen was Dhoni-quick there. Beautifully bowled leg spinner by Tahir. He lands it full and in line of the stumps, Taylor leans forward to defend it with a straight bat but is beaten by the away spin. He loses his balance a bit in the process as Klaasen breaks the stumps. They appeal and the square leg umpire refers it upstairs. The South African players didn't show much excitement but after watching the replays on the giantscreen, they are now celebrating. Superb delivery and equally great glovework to break the 73-run stand.
Stumping appeal! It has been referred upstairs. Not much excitement shown by the Protean players. Let's wait for the replays.
Flighted ball, Williams strokes it through mid off for a run.
Loopy and very full on off, Taylor plays the reverse sweep but finds short third man.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Oohhh... A flighted ball spinning away from around middle and off, Williams gets back to hit it across the line but ends up hitting it onto his pads.
The length is very full this time, around off and Taylor forces it down to long on for one.
Helps it off his pads to mid-wicket and crosses for a run.
Flighted and on off, defended off the back foot.
Tabraiz Shamsi into the attack again.

FOUR! What a way to reach 6000 ODI runs for Brendan Taylor! Tahir floats it up in the air outside off, at 83 kph, Taylor goes down on one knee and slog sweeps it over mid-wicket for a powerful boundary. Becomes the third and quickest Zimbabwean batsman to reach this mark.
Shortish and on off, it's punched from the crease through covers and Zondo in the deep makes a sliding stop. A brace added to the total.
Allows the ball to spin back in from around middle and whips it in front of square leg for a run.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Excellent shot by Brendan. Tahir bowls a leg spinner but down the leg side, it's quite full in length and Taylor unfurls a beautiful paddle sweep for a boundary at fine leg.
Flighted ball outside off, it's pushed through covers for a run.
Tossed up ball on off, Taylor prods forward in defense.

FOUR! Up and over! A good calculative risk taken by Taylor. He knows the fielder is up at mid off and hence plays the aerial shot over him to find the fence. Good use of the feet there by him. 100 up for Zimbabwe, they are looking a lot better now.
A full toss on this occasion, around off, Sean knocks it down to long off for a run.
Brings out the reverse sweep this time but finds the fielder standing at short third man.

FOUR! Fine shot! Slightly overpitched by Duminy this time, it's outside off and Sean drills his drive through the gap at covers for a cracking boundary. 50-run stand comes up, a much-needed stand for the Zimbabweans.
Flighted full ball on off, driven back to the bowler off the front foot.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floats it up on off, the batsman strokes it through mid on for a run.

What did that hit? Replay shows it hit nothing! How has that missed the stump. WOW! The googly by Tahir and it is very full on middle, Williams goes for the reverse sweep but misses. The ball pitches and then turns away, goes agonizingly close past the off pole, hits the keeper on the pads and lobs to first slip. Tahir appeals but he is the only one doing so.
The slider this time, Taylor pushes it down to long on for a run.
The googly on off, Taylor tries to flick but is hit high on the pads.
Tosses it up on off, Taylor keeps it out.
Imran Tahir is back on.
The staighter one on off, SW keeps it out off the back foot.
The batsman drives the ball straight down the ground.
Easily punches it down to long on for a run.
A short and outside off ball, Williams misses out there as he slaps it to sweeper cover for a run. He could have hit that anywhere.
Loopy ball on the pads, Williams plays it back to the bowler.
Swept and swept well. In the gap in the square leg region but only a single accounts.
Length outside off, left alone. A better over by Phehlukwayo this time.
Very full on off, it is stroked to mid off.

In the air... but does not carry! Andile rolls his fingers on the ball, Taylor tries to loft it but the ball goes off the outside part towards sweeper cover. Zondo there comes running in but the ball falls short of him. A run taken.
WIDE! A bumper, it is too high though and it has been wided.
On the pads, Williams flicks it through square leg for a run.
Very full on off, Williams strokes it to mid off.
Works it with the angle to fine leg for a run.
Well tossed up ball on off, driven off the front foot but straight to extra cover.
Goes quicker and hits the yorker mark, Williams does well to dig it out.
Lets this one drift with the arm, it's around off and the batsman pushes it back to the bowler.
A lot slower this time as it lands short on off, Williams cuts it off his back foot but finds point.
Quicker and flatter on the pads, worked on the leg side but straight to mid-wicket.
Flighted full ball on middle, defended back to the bowler.
Turns it off his pads to fine leg for a run. 8 from the over, another expensive one by Andile. The partnership is now worth 38.

FOUR! Boom! You cannot afford to bowl short at such pace. Williams is quick enough to pick the length as he goes on the back foot to ride the bounce. Then, he gives it the full whack of his bat and sends it screaming to the deep mid-wicket fence.
Digs in a short ball around off, Taylor stays back and ramps it down to third man. It goes to the fielder in the deep and they take a run.
Shortish ball around leg, Williams hits it across the line through square leg and jogs across to the other end.
Wide! Sprays a length ball way wide outside off. An easy leave for Williams and the umpire stretches his arms.
A bit short and outside off, it's punched off the back foot by Williams but straight towards the fielder at cover-point.
Angles across a length ball outside off, Williams defends it watchfully to the off side.
Change of ends for Andile Phehlukwayo. He is starting from over the wicket this time. In his last over, he bowled from 'round the wicket to Sean.
The length is very full on off, Taylor sweeps well but this time finds the short fine leg fielder. A good first over by JP!
Slower through the air this time, full and landing outside off. It turns back in a bit after pitching as Taylor draws forward in defense. Gets a thin inside edge onto the pads.
Full and flighted on off, Taylor brings out the reverse sweep, makes good connection but finds backward point.
Tossed up and very full on this occasion, Williams once again drives and this time beats the diving short cover fielder. An easy run taken.
Goes from 'round the wicket to Williams and bowls a full length ball on off. Sean drives it off his front foot but finds the short cover fielder.
A touch flatter to begin with. Shortish in length on middle and leg, Taylor nudges it behind square leg and takes a single.
JP Duminy to bowl his part-time off spinners.

Drinks! A much-better start for Zimbabwe if you consider the last two games. Still, they have lost three wickets and need the current pair to build a partnership. So far so good from Taylor and Williams. Let's see how they fare in the next phase. South Africa will be eyeing more wickets in the middle period. The pitch looks a good one for batting for a change.
A dot to end! Just one from the over! Back of a length on off, kept out.
Back of a length on off, Williams keeps it out.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.

Another brute of a delivery! Short and it once again surprises Taylor. He is late to duck under it. The ball brushes his shoulder and goes to the keeper. Rabada makes an inquiry but the umpire rejects it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Length around off, Taylor works it to mid-wicket with the angle.

FOUR! Three boundaries in the over and an expensive first by Andile. 12 from it, the most expensive over of the game so far. It is the slower one and it is fuller in length. Williams caresses it through covers, there is a man in the deep but he has no chance.
The slower ball wide outside off, the batsman lets it be.
FOUR! Second boundary in the over! Once again it is on the shorter side, Williams has no qualms in putting that away. He stands tall and strokes it through covers.
Slightly fuller this time outside off, the batsman makes a leave.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Short and on the pads, Williams helps it on its way through backward square leg and the ball races away.
On the shorter side, Williams punches it to covers.
Andile Phehlukwayo is into the attack now.
Back of a length on off, Taylor punches it to mid off.
Hits the length again around off, Taylor gets behind the delivery and blocks.
Back of a length again around off, the batsman defends it out.
Around off, it straightens a touch. Taylor tries to defend but the ball takes the outside edge to point.
On a length around off, the batsman keeps it out.
On the pads, Williams flicks it down to fine leg and gets to the other end.
FOUR! Great way to end the over! A good one for them, 9 from it. This is a loopy delivery on off, Taylor goes down on one knee and sweeps it over mid-wicket. No one in the deep so a boundary.
On the shorter side, Taylor flicks it through mid-wicket and the batsmen take two.
Picks the googly and works it with the spin towards square leg for a run.
Plays the reverse sweep but finds the fielder at point.

Full marks to the bowler there but runs to the batsman! It is tossed up on off, turns a little, enough to take the outside edge. Goes past first slip and the batsmen take two. 50 up for Zimbabwe, they have lost three wickets and the run rate is also not great.
Floats it up on off, it is played to covers.
Now steams in from over the wicket to the right-hander. Taylor keeps it out.
Three runs! Through the vacant mid on area! Rabada goes full but ends up bowling a half volley. Williams plays it through mid on. It is not well timed and hence does not get to the rope. Three taken.
Back of a length around middle, cramping the batsman for room. He defends it onto the ground.
Slightly shorter this time, Williams pushes it to mid off.
Another length ball around off, Williams keeps it out.
Comes from around the wicket and bowls it on a length around off, it is kept out. A short leg is in place, so Williams will be tested out with some short ones.
Tossed up ball on off, Taylor keeps it out.
The quicker one but on the shorter side, Taylor tries to flick but misses to get hit high on the pads.
The googly on off, Williams tries to defend but the ball goes off the inner half towards square leg for a run.
Floats it up on off, Williams strokes it to mid off.
This is eased down to long on for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Sean Williams is the new man in.

OUT! A snorter to get rid of Masakadza! Not a lot Hamilton could do there. Rabada sets him up excellently. The previous two balls were very full and this one he bangs in short. It is also well-directed and bowled at a good pace (144 kph). Hamilton is caught by surprise. He tries to fend at it but the ball kisses the gloves and lobs towards the keeper. Klaasen there dives forward and across to take it as the ball was dying in front. Good anticipation by the keeper. Big blow to Zimbabwe. Their skipper was looking good out there and he walks back after getting yet another start. His scores in this series - 25, 27 and 28.
Goes for a yorker but ends up bowling a low full toss. It tails back in also. Hamilton tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
Very full on middle, Masakadza tries to put bat on ball but it goes off the inner half through square leg for a couple.
Another bumper on off, Hamilton evades it.
On a length around off, Masakadza on the up, strokes it to covers.
Driven through mid off by the batsman.
Powerplay 2 has been signaled. Now 4 fielders can be placed outside the ring till the 40th over.
FOUR! Good way to end Powerplay 1. 7 from Shamsi's first. This is floated up on off, Taylor strokes it through covers and the ball races away.
Flighted ball on middle, Taylor tries to read the turn off the pitch and at the very last moment, he gets his bat down and deflects it towards square leg.
Brings out the reverse sweep but does not connect well, finds point.
Another loopy ball on middle, Masakadza chips it towards long on for a single.
Tosses this one up on middle, Taylor works it through square leg for a run
A poor start by him, a long-hop on middle, Hamilton goes back and pulls it towards wide long on for a single.
Tabraiz Shamsi is into the attack. So a double change by South Africa.
Lands it on a length on off, it's punched off the back foot to the off side but the cover fielder dives across to his right to stop the ball. They cross for a run.
Serves it on a length just around off, Masakadza is forward in defense but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Fuller and on off, driven back off the inside half of the blade.
Watchfully leaves a length delivery in the zone outside off.
FOUR! A delightful cover drive by Masakadza. It's served on a length around off, Hamilton is forward as he forces it through the gap on the off side for a boundary.
Starts the spell with a good length delivery in the channel outside off, holding its line, Masakadza shoulders arms.
Kagiso Rabada is introduced into the attack, replacing Dale Steyn. A wide first slip in place.
Top edge but safe! Masakadza brings out the sweep shot but he gets a top edge towards the deep square leg region for a run.
Another googly, this time it turns ever so slightly. Masakadza keeps it out.

DROPPED! A tough chance though. It had to stick. More of a reaction catch you can say. Hamilton uses his feet and dances down the track. Tahir bowls it slower on off, he hits it hard back towards the bowler. Tahir at first tries to take evasive action but then sticks his hand up. The ball brushes his fingers and goes down towards long off for a couple.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Loud shout but it is bat first. The front of the hand delivery, Masakadza goes for the reverse sweep, he does manage to get some glove on it and it goes towards third man for a couple. The players appeal as they feel it has hit the pad but the umpire does not agree and rightly so.
Flatter on off, kept out.
A dot to end the over which went for 9 runs but also produced a wicket. Length outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Off the mark in style! A little too straight there by Steyn, Taylor watchfully flicks it through square leg and the ball races to the fence.
Brendan Taylor walks in next.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Steyn gets the better of Ervine once again. Two-in-two for him against the left-hander. The angle does him in there. Steyn bowls a back of a length delivery around off, it moves away with the angle. Due to the original trajectory, Erive is drawn into the stroke. He ends up playing away from his body. The ball takes the outside edge and goes into the mitts of the keeper. He takes it and appeals and the finger goes up. Craig does not trouble the scorers and Zimbabwe are in trouble once again.
Another length ball outside off, left alone.
Now does the smart thing by guiding this down to third man and getting to the other end.
FOUR! TOP SHOT! Cross-seam delivery but a tad fuller. Masakadza stands tall and strokes it towards mid on. The fielder dives but can't cut it off, it races to the fence. Looking good is Masakadza.
The googly to welcome the left-hander. Ervine blocks it. End of a successful over by Tahir.
Craig Ervine is the new man in.

OUT! Timber and Imran Tahir is off! What a beauty. First real sign of some turn and Tahir gets the better of the batsman. Another tossed up delivery, slower through the air on middle, it pitches and turns slightly. Mire not anticipating any, plays inside the line, the ball goes past his outside edge and uproots the off pole. He walks back for another low score and South Africa draw first blood, early.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Mire goes for the sweep, a shot which he prefers. However, he gets an inside edge onto his boot.
Flatter on middle, Mire punches it to mid on.
Floats it up on off, no spin on offer as of now for Tahir. Mire lunges and easily defends it.
Two dots to end! On a length around off, kept out.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Nicely timed but once again good fielding on display! Fuller in length on off, Masakadza times it towards covers. Zondo there dives and gets a hand on the ball. He takes the sting out of it and saves two for his side.
A bumper on the body of the batsman, it hurries onto him. Mire goes for the pull but mistimes it towards square leg for a run.
Misfield and bonus runs for Zimbabwe! It is on a length around off, Mire pushes it towards covers. The fielder there misreads the bounce and it goes through his hands for a brace.
Good length around off, it skids through after pitching. Mire gets his bat down a touch late, the ball hits the bottom and goes on the bounce to second slip.
Another single to end the over! As Mire strokes it down to long on to retain strike.
Flighted ball on the stumps, Mire lunges and blocks it out.
A low full toss on middle, Masakadza eases it down to long on for another single. Good batting by the two, they are ticking along quite well till now.
A lot of intent on that shot but just a single. It was tossed up by Imran Tahir on middle, Mire swings hard but it goes off the inner half towards long on for a run.
Slightly shorter outside off, Mire punches it through covers for a brace.
Another googly on off, kept out.
Fuller again on off, Masakadza pushes it to mid off.
Driven through mid on by the batsman.
Change in pace there, the slower one on off, Masakadza does well to pick it and stroke it to mid off.

Lovely effort by Markram! He saves a boundary there. Another length delivery on off, Masakadza punches it towards cover-point. As soon as he hits it, he thought runs are on offer here but Markram at point, dives like super man to his right and stops it. Brilliant.

FOUR! TOP SHOT! The first boundary comes off the bat of Hamilton! On the shorter side, Masakadza stands tall and punches it through covers. A test of the outfield and it is lightning quick as the ball races away.
Shorter in length around off, Masakadza defends it.

Another huge appeal! This one is closer than the last one. It is the flipper on middle, Mire goes back and tries to flick but misses. He is hit on the pads. Tahir makes a loud appeal but the umpire does not agree. Height can be the only issue. No reviews however.
Very full on off, Mire pushes it to mid off.

Another googly pitched outside off, Mire kneels down but plants his front foot outside off, he tries to sweep but misses. The ball hits the batsman on the pad. An appeal follows but the umpire is not interested. Outside off the impact.
The googly around off, Mire lunges and keeps it out.
Quicker and flatter again on middle, HM punches it down to long on and gets to the other end.
Flatter and on middle, Masakadza pushes it back to the bowler.
A surprise to begin with by South Africa. A spinner early on. The hat-trick hero of the last game, Imran Tahir to bowl from the other end.
Ends with a dot! Just a run from the first over, a tight one from Steyn. He bowls a straighter line this time. Mire works it to mid-wicket.
Zimbabwe are underway! Goes slightly short this time, Hamilton tries to punch it through the off side but gets an outside edge which goes down to third man for a run.
Gets this ball to come back in after pitching around off and on a length. Masakadza strokes it to mid on. A good start by Steyn so far, 4 balls and all 4 have been bowled around a similar length.
Similar line and length to the last ball. Masakadza once again defends it towards covers.
Closer to the off pole this time, Masakadza confidently defends it towards covers.
Hint of swing there for Steyn but not a lot of bounce on that delivery. He lands it on a length around off, it shapes away a touch. Masakadza makes a leave.

We are done with the national anthems of both teams. The South African players are now taking the field. It's going to be Hamilton Masakadza and Solomon Mire to open for Zimbabwe. Dale Steyn steaming in with the first new ball. Two slips in place. All set, here we go...

Pitch report - Shaun Pollock says there might be some moisture underneath the wicket. He feels it will be a good batting wicket. Reckons there won't be a lot of turn on offer and the spinners will mostly do the containing job.

Brandon Mavuta, who is now giving an interview, says it's coming out really well and he's building confidence with each passing game. Adds that the bowlers are getting the job done and that it's a good thing for the team. States that he takes inspiration from Imran Tahir and there's a lot to learn from someone like him. Mentions that there's some difference in their bowling as he tries to toss it up a lot more while Tahir bowls it slightly quicker with a lot of variations.

Imran Tahir, who is up for an interview, says the hat-trick in the last game was very special. Adds further he is really honored he performed well for the team. Mentions he was not aware about the hat-trick and realized after taking the wicket. Informs he has been working really hard and tries to be as perfect as he can. Admits it was very cold in the last game and is happy it went well. Reckons he gets better by playing in leagues around the world. States the pitches have been tough for batting but the players have done well to get them to a total they can defend. Ends by saying they will look to repeat the last performance.

Faf du Plessis is back to lead South Africa after missing the last two ODIs. He laughs and says it's match fixing if you don't put the camera on the coin. States that he wanted to bat first as well. On losing the toss, he explains that JP Duminy should just come out for the toss as he wins everything. On team changes, he informs there are three changes as him, Kagiso Rabada and Tabraiz Shamsi come in (for Dean Elgar, Lungi Ngidi and Christiaan Jonker). Adds there are two spinners, who are very exciting players and he's waiting to see how they do. Reckons it looks like a really good one-day wicket. Wants it to be a challenge for his bowlers as they try and put the opposition batsmen under pressure. Feels as a team, they are motivated to do better and give it their all. On his injury, he lets everyone know his shoulder is fine and he was just getting tired of sitting on the sidelines.

Zimbabwe skipper, Hamilton Masakadza says the wicket looks a lot better than the other two and he hopes they can put some runs on the board. Informs he is going with the same team. He feels with the different conditions here their batsmen can put in a better performance. Ends by saying they will look to come out all guns blazing and hopes that they can push their opposition a little.
Toss - Up goes the coin and Hamilton Masakadza calls it right. ZIMBABWE ELECT TO BAT!

Hello and welcome to the third and final ODI of the series between South Africa and Zimbabwe. A dead rubber as the hosts have already taken an unassailable lead. A whitewash is what they will be looking for. The visitors on the other hand, will look to salvage some pride with a win here today. The series till now has been dominated by the bowlers as the wickets have not been too conducive for batting. Will we see a similar wicket today? Well, we will have to wait to find out. Stay tuned for further updates.
